name: The Continuous Close
title: The Continuous Close
answer: The continuous close is the practice of keeping a company's books close to final at all times rather than treating month end as a cliff. Instead of a burst of reconciliation, adjustment and review in the last few days of a period, the work is spread across the month so that a trial balance is never far from being reportable. It sits inside financial reporting and synthesis, and it touches the same records that feed statutory reporting, management accounts and audit. The aim is not a faster close for its own sake but a shorter distance between a transaction and its accounting treatment.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: The continuous close is the practice of keeping a company's books close to final at all times rather than treating month end as a cliff. Instead of a burst of reconciliation, adjustment and review in the last few days of a period, the work is spread across the month so that a trial balance is never far from being reportable. It sits inside financial reporting and synthesis, and it touches the same records that feed statutory reporting, management accounts and audit. The aim is not a faster close for its own sake but a shorter distance between a transaction and its accounting treatment.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: A continuous close runs on the general ledger and the subledgers that feed it, plus the reconciliation, matching and journal entry tools layered on top. Most organisations already hold the raw material in an ERP system, a bank feed, a billing platform and a consolidation tool, and the constraint is usually the manual glue between them. Automation arrives through scheduled data pulls, rules for matching, and increasingly through models that classify transactions or flag anomalies for a human to review.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by shortening the cycle rather than compressing it. Transactions are coded and matched as they arrive, reconciliations run on a schedule instead of at period end, and exceptions are routed to an owner while the context is still fresh. Controllers review a rolling set of accounts and investigate movements as they appear, which turns flux analysis from a retrospective exercise into a running one. AI enters mainly at the edges: suggesting account codes, matching payments to invoices, drafting variance commentary, and surfacing items that look unlike their peers. The judgement about what is materially correct stays with the accountant.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Continuous close changes the evidence trail, because a figure may be adjusted many times before it is reported. Teams need clear rules on who can post, what gets locked and when, and how a change is logged so that an auditor can reconstruct the path from source document to final number. Where models propose a coding or a match, the basis for that suggestion should be recorded and reviewable, and the same controls that apply to a manual journal should apply to an automated one.Provenance, versioning and segregation of duties are the practical safeguards.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward a close that is less an event and more a state, with reporting available on demand and the period end reserved for judgement rather than assembly. That shift depends less on better models than on cleaner data, tighter controls and finance teams willing to change when the work happens. Adoption will be uneven, since a continuous close demands discipline every day rather than effort in one week, and many organisations will run a hybrid for years. The likely result is that routine matching and reconciliation fade into the background while review, explanation and judgement become the visible work of the finance function.
